decisions.reason: Both g_1=indicator_[0,infinity) and g_2=-x on [0,infinity), +infinity outside, are proper closed convex and initially removable with f_0=0. Deleting g_1 first retains g_2, whose strict feasible points are x>0; deleting g_2 first retains g_1, whose value is always zero on its domain, so Slater fails. The former definition therefore did not determine its own Slater predicate. Specify smallest original index at every deletion, recompute on the retained family, stop when none is removable, and relabel in original order. Each deletion still preserves D and feasibility. This is a defective definition (other), rather than a failed proof inference.
